intent: Bring linux_configuration/tests/test_security_hardening.sh under the 250-line cap without changing a single assertion or its result, and finish the meta/scripts/mutate_session_autopsy_hooks.py split that a previous session left half-applied and broken in the working tree.
scope: Non-goal: changing, weakening, skipping or deleting any test
Non-goal: fixing the one pre-existing failure this suite reports on this host
changes: Moved the five top-level test sections into three sourced libs, each section wrapped in a function and invoked from the entry script in the original order, so execution order is unchanged.
Kept the entry filename, since .github/workflows/shell-tests.yml runs this suite by filename.
Counters (PASS/FAIL/SKIP) and LIVE_SECTION still live in the entry script; sourcing shares the shell, so the libs mutate them exactly as the former top-level blocks did.

Added a live_section() setter in the entry script and routed the libs' LIVE_SECTION writes through it. Linted in isolation a bare assignment reads as SC2034, since its only reader (test_result) is in the entry file; the setter makes the write a real reference instead of a suppression.

Finished the mutate_session_autopsy_hooks.py split found half-applied in the working tree: the mutation operators had been moved to _session_autopsy_mutations.py but the driver still referenced Mutation without importing it, so mypy and pylint both failed with undefined-variable and the file could not have been committed as left.

LIBS CLEAN - no SC2034, no suppressions added
SHFMT CLEAN. The pre-split entry was already shfmt-dirty; the new files are clean and were not made dirty.

verification.evidence: OUTPUT BYTE-IDENTICAL PRE/POST SPLIT after normalising the repo path prefix. Both runs: Passed 18 / Failed 1 / Skipped 5, both exit 1. The single failure is pre-existing and unrelated to this split.

verification.evidence: ruff, ruff format, mypy, pylint, bandit and pytest-with-coverage all Passed after the missing Mutation import was restored; the mutation hook itself reports PASS.

risks: The libs are only valid when sourced from the entry script, which owns the counters, colors and test_result(). Running a lib directly is not supported and never was a use case.
